data.title: bn-3a54: perf: projection sync rewrites file state for every unchanged review (seal ui ~2s startup)

data.body: [risk:medium] crates/seal-core/src/projection/mod.rs:951-984 (with the scan loop at 1051-1152): SAVEPOINT sync_all now starts a database transaction before load_stored_file_states performs its SELECT, so under default rollback-journal SQLite the read lock remains held while every review log is counted and hashed. Any concurrent sync that has a pending appended event must write, and RELEASE requires exclusive access; this connection has neither WAL nor a busy timeout, so it can fail immediately with SQLITE_BUSY / database is locked. Because .seal logs are repository-controlled, a large log set widens the lock window and makes this an availability regression in the multi-agent use case. Keep the transaction around only the batched projection writes, or establish WAL/busy retry with equivalent safety, and add a file-backed two-connection test where a slow no-op reader overlaps a growing-log sync. Failure-mode checklist: (1) sync/read/vote/comment commands can abort with database is locked; appended events remain durable but the projection stays stale; (2) validate two readers, reader plus writer, two writers, a pending event, large logs, and an enclosing caller transaction; (3) rollback by reverting the outer savepoint while retaining the no-op file-state shortcut, and rebuild index.db if projection recovery is needed; (4) monitor SQLITE_BUSY counts plus sync and commit latency; (5) input validation is not the control here: bound lock duration and handle concurrency, while including oversized event logs in adversarial tests.

data.reason: risk:medium availability regression: the outer sync savepoint holds a rollback-journal read transaction while hashing every log, so concurrent commands can fail with database is locked; see the finding on crates/seal-core/src/projection/mod.rs:951.

data.body: Fixed in 8b161a0: removed the outer SAVEPOINT entirely. Each changed file commits on its own again (as before this branch), so no lock is held across log hashing. The unchanged-file fast path alone gives the speedup (teapot seal ui 2.03s -> 0.07s).

Verified at target 8b161a076624fb1888e72765755c1b0fbd34519a: the outer sync_all savepoint is removed, so log enumeration, line counting, and prefix hashing no longer occur inside a database transaction. Changed files retain their existing per-file savepoints, and the unchanged fast path still validates line count and the stored prefix hash before comparing byte_count. The reported concurrent SQLITE_BUSY regression is addressed.
